_what: MDPF_SECCLASS data contract: the two enumerations the PRD closes as data (PRD CONTRACTS C-FIELD and C-WRITER). The canonical table is DynamoDB etf-classifications; its existing columns (ticker, asset_class, sub_asset_class, sector, name, management_style) are POSN_ASTTAX's and are not restated here.

instrument_kind.domain: every row of etf-classifications, one row per ticker

definitions.fund: a pooled or exchange-traded product classified by the ETF classes: an ETF, an ETN (e.g. VXX), a mutual fund, or a closed-end fund
definitions.single_security: one issuer's own instrument: a company's common or preferred stock, or a single bond

instrument_kind.absent: a row without instrument_kind is not defaulted to either value; a reader shows the instrument's kind as unknown by name (brief Part III, 'Nothing silently folds')
instrument_kind.ordering_use: a holdings table places every single_security row after the last fund class; the key is produced and served by the backend, never re-derived in the portal (Andrew-direct 2026-09-29 ~19:5xZ, server side)

rule24_record.domain_declared: the rows of etf-classifications (tickers), the population FWD-8's ACCEPT reads
rule24_record.mece_by_subtraction: every row is either pooled/exchange-traded under the ETF classes (fund) or one issuer's instrument (single_security); the remainder after subtracting both is cash and cash-equivalent lines, which are not rows of this table (cash rows are classified by the holdings producers' cash rule, PRD v0.20 rulings of IRPT_BCKEND) -- an unforeseen member reads as absent, never forced
rule24_record.intent_coherence: one axis: what kind of instrument the ticker is; no ordering, class or vendor meaning is carried in it
rule24_record.state_coherence: setting instrument_kind moves no asset_class or sub_asset_class value; the ordering of a table moves only through the served key
rule24_record.token_census: word-boundary census of instrument_kind, 2026-09-29 ~20:1xZ, native Grep: infra/aws/lambda/v2_portal 0 hits, data/**/*.py 0 hits, portal/src 0 hits -- no collision

identifier_namespace.domain: every row of etf-classifications, one row per ticker

definitions.TICKER: the row's ticker column holds an ordinary exchange ticker symbol -- the pre-existing shape of every row before E9, and the default reading for any row where identifier_namespace is absent
definitions.CUSIP: the row's ticker column holds a CUSIP-prefixed key, `"CUSIP:<9 chars>"` (the literal 9-character CUSIP), for a security with no exchange ticker (e.g. a bond); the table gains no new column -- the existing ticker attribute carries the prefixed string

identifier_namespace.absent: a row without identifier_namespace reads as TICKER (CTO RULING 103140); the value is never inferred from the ticker column's own shape (e.g. a leading "CUSIP:" substring) -- it is a stated attribute, not a derived one, so a row's identifier_namespace and its ticker's shape are two carriers that must agree by construction of the writer, never by a reader re-parsing the key

rule24_record.domain_declared: the rows of etf-classifications (tickers), the population E9's CUSIP-keyed write touches
rule24_record.mece_by_subtraction: every row's ticker column holds either an ordinary exchange ticker (TICKER) or a CUSIP-prefixed key (CUSIP); the remainder after subtracting both is empty over this field's own domain -- an absent value reads TICKER, never forced to CUSIP by inference
rule24_record.intent_coherence: one axis: which identifier scheme keys the row; no class, ordering or vendor meaning is carried in it
rule24_record.state_coherence: setting identifier_namespace moves no asset_class, sub_asset_class or classified_by value; a CUSIP row's full identifier lives in the one ticker column, never split across two attributes
rule24_record.token_census: word-boundary census of identifier_namespace, 2026-09-30 ~03:2xZ, native/comp-find: infra/aws/lambda/v2_portal 0 hits, data 0 hits, portal/src 8 hits -- ALL in IRPT_BCKEND's own wire contract (portal/src/pages/InvestorReporting/contracts/wire/AnalysisRequest.ts, adapt.ts, fixtures/tests), whose identifier_namespace enum is wider (TICKER|CUSIP|ISIN|CASH|MODEL|UNMATCHED) and is a DIFFERENT schema (IRPT's own normalized-holdings wire, not etf-classifications) -- same token name, disjoint domain; flagged as row MDPF_SECCLASS-W5-S2, not a write-path collision

definitions.seed: written by the seed path from infra/aws/lambda/v2_portal/_shared/etf_classification.py (the one place a person adds or corrects a row)
definitions.scheduled: written by the scheduled classification of FWD-7 for a ticker that had NO row; the write is conditional on the row's absence, so it never overwrites a seed or constituents row
definitions.constituents: written by infra/aws/lambda/v2_portal/yang_pipeline/seed-etf-constituents.py for a constituent ticker of Opal's own ETFs that had NO row (or carried no label); the write is conditional on the row's absence or its lacking a label, so it never overwrites a seed, scheduled or already-labelled row
definitions.legacy: not written by any path: a missing label reads as legacy. It means the row predates this contract and its provenance was not recorded -- it is not a claim about which seeder wrote it, and it never overwrites or is written to an existing attribute; it is produced by ONE additive conditional label update (label-legacy-classified-by.py) on rows carrying no classified_by attribute

classified_by.precedence: a seed row always wins: a correction to a scheduled or constituents row is made by adding the ticker to the seed source, and the next seed run replaces the row with classified_by = seed. scheduled and constituents each write ONLY where no row exists (attribute_not_exists(classified_by)), so neither overwrites the other or a seed row. A row with no classified_by attribute reads as legacy until the one label update sets it; legacy therefore loses to seed and to a future scheduled/constituents write (attribute_not_exists still holds against a row that never received a label), and wins against nothing -- it is the read-time default for an absent attribute, not a write that competes for the row.
classified_by.estate_note: the estate's per-firm classifiers already write a free-text classified_by into their own tables (bd-securities: seed_from_yang, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-4o-mini, auto-detected); those tables and their writers retire under FWD-5/FWD-4; on etf-classifications the field takes only the four values above

rule24_record.domain_declared: the writers of etf-classifications rows (and, for rows with no writer of record, the read-time label)
rule24_record.mece_by_subtraction: a row is written by the seed path, the scheduled classification, the constituents path, or -- for a row with none of the three's attribute set -- it reads legacy; any other writer is a copy that FWD-4's census reports
rule24_record.same_grain: one writer (or read-time label) per row
rule24_record.intent_coherence: one axis: which of the three sanctioned write paths wrote the row, or that none did (legacy)
rule24_record.state_coherence: classified_by moves no class value; a seed run over a scheduled, constituents or legacy row changes both classified_by and, where they differ, the class values; the legacy label update (SET classified_by = legacy on attribute_not_exists(classified_by)) moves no other attribute on any row
